```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(MixSIARPFN)
ok <- MixSIARPFN:::networks_ready()   # the code needs the networks (see pfn_networks())
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = ok,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, out.width = "100%")
num <- function(x, digits = 2) if (ok) format(round(x, digits), nsmall = digits) else "?"
```

This follows MixSIAR's snail example script (`mixsiar_script_snail.R`): snails
with one tracer (δ¹³C) and two food sources, C3 and CAM plants, and no effects. Two things make it different from the other examples: there is only one
tracer, and the source data are raw samples rather than means and SDs. Only the
fitting call differs from MixSIAR's script: `run_pfn()` in place of
`write_JAGS_model()` and `run_model()`.

## The data

```{r load, eval = TRUE}
mix <- load_mix_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "snail_consumer.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  iso_names = "d13C", factors = NULL, fac_random = NULL,
  fac_nested = NULL, cont_effects = NULL)
source <- load_source_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "snail_sources.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  source_factors = NULL, conc_dep = FALSE, data_type = "raw", mix)
discr <- load_discr_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "snail_discrimination.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  mix)
```

With `data_type = "raw"`, `load_source_data()` summarises each source's samples to
its mean, SD and sample size, which is what MixSIARPFN's networks use:

```{r sources, eval = TRUE}
source$data
```

There are `r mix$N` snails.

```{r isospace, eval = TRUE, fig.height = 4}
plot_data(mix = mix, source = source, discr = discr)
```

## Fitting the model

Residual * Process error and MixSIAR's uninformative Dirichlet prior, as in MixSIAR's
script.

```{r fit}
time <- system.time(
  fit <- run_pfn(mix, source, discr, alpha.prior = 1,
                 resid_err = TRUE, process_err = TRUE)
)
fit
```

## Results

```{r output, results = "hide", fig.show = "hide"}
out <- output_pfn(fit, mix, source,
                  output_options = list(summary_save = FALSE, plot_post_save_pdf = FALSE))
```

```{r summary-table}
knitr::kable(round(summary_table(fit), 3))
```

```{r result-plots, fig.height = 4}
out$plots$global
```

The snails' diet is mostly C3 plants. With one tracer and two sources the diet is
well identified: the consumers' δ¹³C sits between the two sources, much closer to C3.
